scope.frame: characters of the free group F_n in SU(2) with finite non-abelian image; the moves a_i -> a_i a_j, a_j a_i (generating SAut(F_n))
scope.object: the weave of n records, n = 2, 3, 4; every finite non-abelian subgroup of SU(2) (Dic_m by census for m <= 15 and by an argument for every m; 2T, 2O, 2I by census)
scope.hypotheses: SU(2) and a finite image are inputs; infinite images and other targets are outside the claim; n >= 5 is not covered

claim_one_line: THE COMMON POINT AND THE COUNT OF RECORDS (sealed 33a40692b before the run; output 2b04ffa80 committed unread; every cell holds): among the characters of F_n in SU(2) with finite non-abelian image, a point fixed by every move of the weave of n records exists only at n = 2 (for n <= 4), where it is unique -- the quaternion point (Q8, traces (0, 0, 0)); at n = 3 and 4 every filtered generating tuple of Q8, 2T and 2I is moved, and the binary dihedral groups have no common point for any m (they force trace zero, which confines the generators to Q8). So the count of two records (GM1) follows from a weaker stated input, that the weave shares a persistent point in SU(2) with finite non-abelian image, and the triplet follows from that point (the paper's T2, T3). The transitivity is known for solvable groups (Dunwoody) and PSL(2, p) (Gilman); the census includes the non-solvable 2I; the reading is the record's. SU(2) and a finite image stay priced; n >= 5 not covered. 0 of 19.
weave_or_thread: weave (every move of the weave of n records, every finite non-abelian image)
